title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VI 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)', June 1986. It is an axiomatic, combinatorial theory of plane 'figures'. The theory has a set L of lines and points, and figures F, G in a family 𝓕. There is an order ≤ ('is a sub-figure of'), a stronger relation ≪ (and ⋘), shadows ombr(F), and axioms labelled At 4, At 9, At 10, At 11'. Figures need not have a supremum. Two figures are called 'compatible' when F ∨ G exists; on this page the symbol written between figures is used in that sense, by the text's own gloss. Inf / Inf'' denote infima, and F'|K := Inf(F', K) is the restriction of F' to K.

Grothendieck wants to strengthen At 11'. Proposed statement (marked '?'): let F, G be compatible figures, K = F ∧ G, H = F ∨ G, and F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G. Then F' and G' are compatible if and only if F'|K and G'|K are compatible. In that case F' ∨ G' ≪ F ∨ G.

Proof attempt.
(1) If H' = F' ∨ G' exists, then H' ≪ H. He says this follows at once from criterion At 4. An earlier attempt via K' = F' ∧ G' ≪ K is struck out.
(2) Necessity: F'|K is a sub-figure of F' ≤ H', hence of H'; likewise G'|K. So both lie in the common figure H' and are compatible.
(3) He sets up a cube. The top face is K ≤ F, G ≤ H; the bottom face is K' ≤ F', G' ≤ H'. The vertical arrows F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G, K' ≪ K, H' ≪ H are 'simple ≪'. Both horizontal faces are cartesian, i.e. meets.
(4) He computes K' = Inf''(F', G') = Inf''(F', G', K) = Inf''(F'|K, G'|K). So the meet of F' and G' is controlled by their restrictions to the overlap K.
(5) The converse (sufficiency) is started ('Inversement, supposons F'|K et G'|K compatibles') and continued on p. 74. There the cube is refined with H'_F, H'_G, H'_K, F'_K, G'_K, and the horizontal squares are required to be both cartesian and cocartesian.

In modern terms this is a gluing / amalgamation criterion in a partial lattice of subobjects. Two 'interior' sub-figures of F and G can be amalgamated inside F ∨ G iff they agree (are compatible) on the overlap F ∧ G. It reads like a sheaf or van Kampen-type gluing condition for a bicartesian square of sub-figures, used to build up the axiomatics of elementary plane topology.
errors: The statement is explicitly marked 'Proposition (?)', so Grothendieck himself is unsure; only the easy directions are sketched on this page.
Step H' ≪ H is justified only by 'résulte aussitôt de At 4' without detail; a previous attempt (via K' ≪ K) was struck out.
Sufficiency (compatibility on K implies compatibility of F', G') is not proved here; it needs the cartesian/cocartesian cube completed on p. 74.
Large parts of the page are crossed out with diagonal strokes, so the surviving argument is fragmentary.

ideas.what: Gluing criterion: sub-figures F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G are compatible (have a join) iff their restrictions to K = F ∧ G are compatible, and then F' ∨ G' ≪ F ∨ G
ideas.modern_name: amalgamation / gluing condition on overlaps in a partial lattice of subobjects (sheaf-like or Mayer–Vietoris-type square)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard pattern (sheaf gluing; amalgamation in lattice theory)
ideas.where_published: Analysis situs notes unpublished; theme of an axiomatic 'tame' topology is only alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Cube of figures with cartesian (meet) horizontal faces and ≪ vertical arrows; K' = Inf''(F'|K, G'|K)
ideas.modern_name: morphism of pullback squares / bicartesian squares of subobjects

missed.claim: This is part of an unpublished 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs' of plane figures (lines, shadows, relations ≪, axioms At 1–At 11'). The page attempts a gluing proposition strengthening At 11'. The whole axiomatic programme, an attempt at a combinatorial foundation of tame plane topology, has not been developed in the literature.
missed.quote: J'ai envie de renforcer At 11', dans la direction suivante : Proposition (?) ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest as part of Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme; the specific gluing lemma itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine gluing/amalgamation lemma in a private axiomatic framework, left marked '?'. It is interesting only as evidence of the 1986 analysis-situs programme, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: The relation symbol written between F and G (and between F', G' and F'|K, G'|K) is glossed by the text itself as 'compatible' (i.e. F ∨ G exists). The transcription renders it '≭' with '[?]'; it should be read as a compatibility relation, not 'not equivalent'.
'crition At 4' is probably 'critère At 4' ('cela résulte aussitôt du critère At 4').

The line '— les 8 flèches horizontales sont des ≤, et les quatre flèches verticales des ≪ simples' is not individually struck through. It lies under the large diagonal cancellation strokes covering the middle/lower part of the page, which also cross out the diagram and the Inf'' computation.
The line 'Ils sont compatibles' is more likely the start of a cancelled sentence 'Ils sont compatibles ... car ...'. Similarly, '... un diagramme ...' near the diagram is struck.
